text: A registered trade mark is infringed by a person who, not being a registered proprietor or permitted user, uses in the course of trade a mark which is identical or deceptively similar to the trade mark in relation to identical or similar goods or services, causing public confusion or likelihood of association. Sub-section (4) protects well-known trademarks against dilution and unfair advantage even for dissimilar goods. Jurisdiction lies under Section 134 before District Court where plaintiff resides or carries on business.

marginal_heading: Common Law Remedy for Passing Off Preserved
text: No person is entitled to institute proceedings for infringement of an unregistered trade mark. However, Section 27(2) explicitly preserves the common law tort of Passing Off. An action for passing off lies where plaintiff establishes: (1) goodwill or reputation attached to his goods/services; (2) misrepresentation by defendant leading public to believe defendant's goods are plaintiff's; (3) actual or probable damage (Reckitt & Colman Classical Trinity).

Copyright in a work shall be deemed to be infringed when any person, without a license granted by the owner, does anything the exclusive right to do which is conferred upon the owner, or permits for profit any place to be used for the communication of the work to the public where such communication constitutes infringement. Civil remedies under Section 55 include injunctions, damages, and delivery up of infringing copies; criminal penalties under Section 63 include mandatory minimum 6 months imprisonment.

Certain acts do not constitute infringement of copyright: (a) Fair dealing with any work (not being computer programme) for private use, research, criticism or review, reporting of current events; (b) making of copies by teachers or pupils in course of instruction; (c) performance in course of activities of educational institution; (d) reproduction for judicial proceedings or report thereof (Delhi University Photocopying judgment ratio).

marginal_heading: What are Not Inventions (Section 3(d) Evergreening Bar & Section 3(k) Software Bar)
text: The following are not inventions under Indian patent law: Section 3(d) bars mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in enhancement of known therapeutic efficacy (Novartis Gleevec Supreme Court doctrine); Section 3(k) bars mathematical methods, business methods, computer programmes per se or algorithms; Section 3(m) bars mere scheme or rule or method of performing mental act.

marginal_heading: Penalty and Compensation for Damage to Computer, Data Theft, & Cyber Trespass
text: If any person without permission of owner secures access to computer system, downloads, copies or extracts any data, introduces computer contaminant/virus, damages or disrupts computer system, denies access to authorized person, or steals source code, he is liable to pay damages by way of compensation to affected person up to Rs. 5 crore adjudicated by State IT Secretary as Adjudicating Officer under Section 46.

marginal_heading: Punishment for Identity Theft & Digital Impersonation
text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to Rs. 1 lakh. Cognizable offence under Section 77B.

marginal_heading: Intermediary Safe Harbor & Due Diligence Requirements
text: An intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by him provided: (a) intermediary function is limited to providing access; (b) intermediary does not initiate transmission, select receiver, or modify information; (c) intermediary observes due diligence under IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021. Under Shreya Singhal Supreme Court doctrine, safe harbor is lost only if intermediary fails to take down unlawful content within 24-36 hours upon receiving actual knowledge via Court Order or Government Notification.
